newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends listless session near its lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends listless session near its lows.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a listless session near its lows on Wednesday after trading a 20 basis point range.
At 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) the Kiwi was at US$0.7039/46 from a 0.7053/60 opening, having traded a 0.7038-58 range. On its Trade-Weighted Index it finished at 67.32 against its 67.52 open.
Dealers said local buying took the Kiwi up to its highs in the morning but selling out of Tokyo in the afternoon saw it weaken off to support levels.
They said Japanese players appeared to be taking profits and were generally selling on the crosses following the U.S. dollar's strong run against the yen.

Financial markets took little notice of a fracas involving New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, who did not attend talks between his party and both the National and Labour Parties over the formation of a coalition.
Dealers said Labour appeared to have got a foot in the door over forming a government after being on the back foot last week. Separate talks with both parties continue on Thursday.
